text:
Marta: Quick sync — trying to lock down the benchmark methodology for the kernel-selection and batching perf work. Goal: apples-to-apples across replay vs synthetic runs, and stable CI alerts.
Alex: Short version: replay for realistic distribution, synthetic for corner stress. But make sure both use the same model binary + kernel map + quant settings.
Priya: Agreed. We should also pin sequence-length distributions and temperature/stop rules for generation. Otherwise perf apples-to-apples is meaningless.
Liam: Important: KV cache state. We need a warmup routine. Measure cold, warm, and steady-state separately. I propose: 100 trace warmup requests, then 1k measured requests. If cache hit < 85% during measured window, mark as "warmup insufficient".
Marta: +1. Put that into the harness. Also add a step to report cache-hit histogram.
Alex: Here's a minimal load command I'm using for synthetic runs:
```
# run synthetic stress with pinned kernel map
./loadgen \
  --model /artifacts/gptx-v1.bin \
  --kernel-map kernels/v2.3.1.map \
  --concurrency 16 \
  --batch-window-ms 5 \
  --seq-dist sequences/median-512.json
```
Priya: For replay harness we replay real traffic traces but normalize timestamps and client concurrency so we compare throughput/latency at identical offered load. Example: scale factor -> 0.5/1/2 to sweep.
Liam: Batching heuristics: test both continuous batching (always try to fill up to N tokens) and timeout-based microbatching. Log per-batch size distribution. Small detail: kernel selection sometimes flips on particular sequence-length buckets — we need to export which kernel chosen per-request for debug.
Josh: For CI automation, propose this pipeline for nightly and PR smoke:
- nightly: full sweep (replay + synthetic) across 3 scale factors, KV warmup, publish dashboard artifacts.
- PR-smoke: 10min synthetic run with 2 seeds, check 3 key metrics (p50 latency, p95 latency, tokens/sec) against commit baseline.
Marta: What about thresholds/alerts? We saw yesterday a flake where p95 jumped 12% but reverted next run. We need hysteresis: alert if regression > 8% AND persists for 3 consecutive nightly runs or >12% in a PR-smoke.
eng-ci-bot: Automated check: "perf/regression" rule applied. Posting alerts to #eng-runtime-incidents when condition met. Link to dashboard: https://dash.redwood/perf/runs/17673
Priya: Dashboards: publish raw histograms + summary deltas vs baseline commit. Include small text note about kernel_map and quant flags used in that run. This prevents confusion when kernel switching happens.
Alex: Flaky test triage: label flake with `perf:flaky` and auto-disable from blocking if >50% of flake incidents are environmental. Also add deterministic seeds to synthetic runs to reduce nondeterminism.
Liam: Also include a reproducibility artifact: tarball with model binary, kernel map, trace subset, and the exact loadgen command. Store with run metadata (sha, kernel-map-hash).
Marta: Action items:
- Priya: add KV warmup + cache hist reporting to harness (due EOD Thu)
- Alex: add kernel-choice export (per-request) and integrate into dashboard (due Fri)
- Josh: update CI workflow (nightly + PR-smoke + alert hysteresis) and add eng-ci-bot rule (due Mon)
- Liam: add reproducibility artifact writer to run steps (due Fri)
Josh: I'll draft the GH action for PR-smoke today and ping for review.
Priya: one more: include a small statistical test for the comparison (KS test on latency histograms) — if p < 0.01 flag for manual review.
Marta: Nice. If anyone hits a flaky false-positive, annotate run with `env-note` and we'll skip it for 3 runs while we investigate.
Alex: Thanks all — this should make kernel/batching regression detection way less noisy. :tada:
eng-ci-bot: CI job started: `nightly-perf-sweep/1767304821`. Artifacts will be available at https://ci.redwood/artifacts/1767304821
Marta: I'll follow up with a short doc summarizing the methodology and put links in the dashboard.
Liam: Quick reminder: when comparing kernel v2 vs v3, also check CPU fallback paths (we had a silent fallback incident last quarter). Add an explicit check for binary fallback in harness.
Marta: Cool — closing thread for now. Post updates here as PRs land.
